title: Born-digital report
shows: A text layer made with the document: the cheap rule trusts it, so OCR and vision are skipped.

title: Paper with equations
shows: Born-digital, but full of mathematical notation, which needs a math-aware lane.

title: Source listing
shows: A monospaced code page: complex layout although the text layer is clean.
source: Own construction; CPython source under the PSF License

title: Clean scan
shows: An image with no text layer, sharp and flat: OCR will read it as it is.

title: Mildly degraded copy
shows: The same page with light digital degradation. Borderline between L3 and L4, so review may catch it.

title: Photographed printout
shows: The same page again, photographed on a desk: a degraded capture.

title: Camera photo
shows: A synthetic phone photo: perspective, vignette and blur.

title: Fax
shows: A synthetic fax: dithered, skewed and speckled.

title: Handwriting
shows: A photo of handwritten notes: the vision check sees handwriting, Jev routes it to L5.

title: Arabic page
shows: A clean page in Arabic script: the script and right-to-left modifiers ride along with the lane.

title: Three-page PDF
shows: A born-digital page, a table page and a faxed page with an old OCR layer: three segments in one manifest.

title: Word document
shows: A native office file: no rendering needed, so it goes straight to L0.

title: Zip archive
shows: A container: intake expands it, and each file inside is routed as its own document.

title: Email with attachment
shows: The body text is native (L0); the attached two-column PDF is routed on its own.
source: Own construction; attachment from olmOCR-Bench (allenai/olmOCR-bench), ODC-By 1.0

title: Encrypted PDF
shows: Password protected, so intake quarantines it with a reason instead of guessing.
